subject: Uptime measurement alignment & credit trigger proposal - Order Form redline
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@stellarsys.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellarsys.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines on uptime measurement + credit triggers

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We reviewed the Order Form and had our legal/ops teams mark up the SLA. The main open items are: how uptime is measured (per-region vs. global), rolling maintenance windows and blackout periods, and the exact credit calculation when the uptime threshold is missed.

I attached the PDF with inline comments and proposed language. High level asks:
- Make uptime measurement region-specific (we want per-region availability).
- Cap on aggregate credits per 12-month period.
- Clear exclusion for scheduled maintenance but narrower definition so we can’t exceed 4 hours/month without credits.

Can you loop in Redwood legal and ops to confirm whether your monitoring/metrics can emit region-level uptime and whether your maintenance policy can align with our blackouts? We need final redline by Monday to hit our internal procurement cadence.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Infrastructure, StellarSys
[Attachment: StellarSLA_redline_20271020.pdf]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@stellarsys.com>
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines on uptime measurement + credit triggers

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary and the annotated redlines. Looping in Rafael (legal) and Kimberly (ops) to validate measurement definitions and credit language. A few quick notes from product side:
- We can emit per-region uptime metrics; the platform supports region-level SLOs, but need to confirm the exact aggregation window you expect (rolling 30d vs. calendar month).
- Scheduled maintenance currently has a monthly aggregate cap we can make explicit; we will propose wording to align with your 4 hours/month ask but need to preserve emergency patch carve-outs.
- Credits: Redwood typically proposes a sliding credit scale tied to monthly availability; happy to propose a cap and an annual aggregate.

Targeting internal alignment today so we can provide a counter-redline by EOD and a final by Monday.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@stellarsys.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redlines on uptime measurement + credit triggers

Lauren / Jordan —

Thanks for the context. Per legal review, proposed language below (high level) — I included alternatives where we think negotiation will land. Please let me know which you prefer so I can produce a tracked-change redline.

1) Measurement scope - Option A (preferred): "Availability shall be measured separately for each Deployment Region using Redwood's monitoring systems and reported as the percentage of successful request responses over the applicable Measurement Window."
- Option B: Global measurement with per-region reporting for transparency (Jordan: we expect you to prefer A).

2) Maintenance / Blackouts - Redwood accepts Scheduled Maintenance exclusions up to 4 hours per calendar month per region. Scheduled Maintenance must be notified 72 hours in advance and scheduled outside of Customer's announced blackout windows where commercially reasonable. Emergency maintenance (security patches) may be performed with best-effort notice and is excluded from the 4 hour cap.

3) Credits and cap - Sliding scale (example):
  - >= 99.95%: No credits
  - 99.9% - 99.949%: 10% monthly service fee credit
  - 99.5% - 99.899%: 25% monthly service fee credit
  - < 99.5%: 50% monthly service fee credit
- Aggregate cap: Credits for all regions combined shall not exceed 100% of one (1) month of fees in any rolling 12-month period.

4) Measurement window - Propose rolling 30-day window for calculation to avoid calendar month edge cases; open to calendar month if that is a strict procurement requirement.

Please confirm the credit cap (we propose one month / 12-month rolling cap) and whether StellarSys needs calendar month windows. Once confirmed we'll provide a tracked draft for the Order Form.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_sla_snippet.txt]

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@stellarsys.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellarsys.com>, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines on uptime measurement + credit triggers

Rafael / Lauren —

This looks reasonable and close to what we need. Two clarifications before I send back to procurement:
1) We prefer calendar-month measurement for internal billing simplicity. Is there any technical blocker to doing calendar-month vs. rolling 30-day?
2) For Emergency maintenance carve-out, can we get a definition that requires Redwood to provide "as soon as practicable" notice and a post-incident summary within 5 business days?

If legal can accept calendar-month wording and the 5-day post-incident summary, Procurement will take the draft as-is and we can proceed to a final tracked Order Form and DocuSign.

I'll await the updated snippet. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Jordan
Head of Infrastructure, StellarSys
[Attachment: OrderForm_draft_SStemplate.docx]
